title: Blood flow through the heart and the two circulations
blurb: Put every chamber, valve and great vessel in order, and explain why pulmonary veins carry oxygenated blood.
question: A red blood cell returns from the leg through the inferior vena cava. In order, which chambers, valves and vessels does it pass through before it leaves the heart again in the aorta?

teach.body: Formally, the pulmonary circulation carries blood from the right ventricle to the lungs and back to the left atrium; the systemic circulation carries blood from the left ventricle to the body and back to the right atrium. In plain English: the right side of the heart sends tired blood to the lungs to pick up oxygen, and the left side sends that fresh blood out to every tissue. Each loop ends where the other begins.

teach.h: Body to lungs: the right heart
Lungs to body: the left heart
teach.caption: In the body: arteries, arterioles, capillaries, venules, veins, then back to the venae cavae.
Follow the numbers 1 to 13: that is the order one drop of blood takes, through the right side, out to the lungs, then back through the left side.

teach.h: Direction, not oxygen, names the vessel
teach.body: Arteries carry blood AWAY from the heart; veins carry blood TOWARD it, whatever its oxygen level. Usually arteries carry oxygenated blood, but the pulmonary arteries carry deoxygenated blood from the right ventricle to the lungs, and the pulmonary veins carry oxygenated blood back to the left atrium. The fetus shows the same rule: umbilical arteries carry deoxygenated blood and the umbilical vein carries oxygenated blood.

teach.caption: Note the pulmonary vein: it carries oxygen-rich blood, yet it is a vein because it flows toward the heart.

teach.h: Arteries and veins, with the exceptions

teach.body: The myocardium cannot use the blood inside its chambers. It is supplied by the left and right coronary arteries, which branch from the base of the aorta just above the aortic valve and fill mainly during diastole. Coronary veins drain into the coronary sinus, which empties into the right atrium. A blocked coronary artery starves the heart muscle of oxygen: a myocardial infarction (heart attack).

teach.h: Scenario: Luis traces a red blood cell
teach.body: Luis, studying for the TEAS, traces one red blood cell from his toe. It rides the veins to the inferior vena cava, enters the right atrium, crosses the tricuspid valve into the right ventricle, then exits through the pulmonary valve into the pulmonary trunk and arteries. After loading O₂ in the lungs, it returns in a pulmonary vein to the left atrium, crosses the mitral valve, and leaves the left ventricle through the aortic valve into the aorta.

teach.text: Pulmonary VEINS carry OXYGENATED blood and pulmonary ARTERIES carry DEOXYGENATED blood. Defining an artery as "a vessel with oxygenated blood" is the trap: the definition is direction. Also, blood leaves the right ventricle through the pulmonary trunk, never the aorta.

items: Pulmonary circulation: RV to lungs to LA. Systemic circulation: LV to body to RA.
Right heart order: venae cavae, RA, tricuspid, RV, pulmonary valve, pulmonary trunk.
Left heart order: pulmonary veins, LA, mitral, LV, aortic valve, aorta.
Arteries go away from the heart, veins toward it, regardless of oxygen.
Coronary arteries leave the aortic base; coronary veins drain via the coronary sinus to the RA.
Hepatic portal vein: gut, spleen and pancreas blood goes to the liver first.

summary: You can now put every chamber, valve and great vessel in order around both circulations and define arteries and veins by direction. You can also explain the pulmonary vessel exception, the coronary circulation and the hepatic portal system.

A.q: Which vessel carries oxygenated blood from the lungs to the heart?
options: Pulmonary artery
Pulmonary vein
Superior vena cava
Aorta
A.why: Pulmonary veins return freshly oxygenated blood from the lungs to the left atrium.

whyNot.0: Pulmonary arteries carry deoxygenated blood AWAY from the heart to the lungs.
whyNot.2: The superior vena cava returns deoxygenated blood from the upper body to the right atrium.
whyNot.3: The aorta carries oxygenated blood AWAY from the heart to the body.

A.q: After leaving the left atrium, blood passes next through the:
options: Tricuspid valve
Aortic valve
Pulmonary valve
Mitral valve
A.why: Blood goes from the left atrium through the mitral (bicuspid) valve into the left ventricle.

whyNot.0: The tricuspid valve is on the right side, between the RA and RV.
whyNot.1: The aortic valve is crossed later, as blood leaves the left ventricle.
whyNot.2: The pulmonary valve is the exit from the RIGHT ventricle.

A.q: The systemic circulation begins as blood leaves which chamber?
options: Left ventricle
Right ventricle
Left atrium
Right atrium
A.why: The left ventricle pumps blood into the aorta, starting the systemic circulation to the body.

whyNot.1: The right ventricle starts the PULMONARY circulation.
whyNot.2: The left atrium is where the pulmonary circulation ends.
whyNot.3: The right atrium is where the systemic circulation ends.

B.q: Which statement correctly defines an artery?
options: A vessel that carries oxygenated blood
A vessel that carries blood toward the heart
A vessel that carries blood away from the heart
A vessel that carries blood at the lowest pressure
B.why: Arteries are defined by direction: they carry blood away from the heart, whether or not it is oxygenated.

whyNot.0: Pulmonary arteries carry deoxygenated blood, so oxygen content cannot be the definition.
whyNot.1: Carrying blood toward the heart defines a vein.
whyNot.3: Arteries carry blood at the HIGHEST pressure; the lowest pressures are found in veins.

B.q: The coronary arteries branch from the:
options: Base of the aorta, just above the aortic valve
Pulmonary trunk, just above the pulmonary valve
Coronary sinus in the right atrium wall
Left ventricle, just below the aortic valve
B.why: The left and right coronary arteries arise from the base of the aorta, just above the aortic valve.

whyNot.1: The pulmonary trunk carries deoxygenated blood to the lungs; it does not supply the heart.
whyNot.2: The coronary sinus collects venous blood from the heart and drains into the right atrium.
whyNot.3: Arteries do not branch from inside a ventricle; the coronaries leave the aorta above the valve.

B.q: Blood from the stomach and intestines travels to the liver through the:
options: Inferior vena cava
Coronary sinus
Abdominal aorta branches
Hepatic portal vein
B.why: The hepatic portal vein carries blood from the stomach, intestines, spleen and pancreas to the liver before it returns to the heart.

whyNot.0: The inferior vena cava returns blood to the right atrium, AFTER the liver.
whyNot.1: The coronary sinus drains the heart muscle into the right atrium.
whyNot.2: Branches of the aorta carry blood TO the gut, not from the gut to the liver.

C.q: A red blood cell has just entered the right atrium. Which sequence does it follow next?
options: Tricuspid valve, right ventricle, aortic valve, aorta
Mitral valve, right ventricle, pulmonary valve, pulmonary trunk
Pulmonary valve, right ventricle, tricuspid valve, pulmonary trunk
Tricuspid valve, right ventricle, pulmonary valve, pulmonary trunk
C.why: From the right atrium, blood crosses the tricuspid valve into the right ventricle, then the pulmonary valve into the pulmonary trunk.

whyNot.0: The right ventricle empties into the pulmonary trunk, not the aorta.
whyNot.1: The mitral valve is on the left side; the right AV valve is the tricuspid.
whyNot.2: The tricuspid valve comes BEFORE the right ventricle and the pulmonary valve after it.

C.q: In an adult, which pair of vessels BOTH carry deoxygenated blood?
options: Pulmonary veins and the venae cavae
Pulmonary arteries and venae cavae
Pulmonary arteries and the aorta
Pulmonary veins and the aorta
C.why: The venae cavae return deoxygenated blood from the body, and the pulmonary arteries carry it from the right ventricle to the lungs.

whyNot.0: Pulmonary veins carry OXYGENATED blood from the lungs to the left atrium.
whyNot.2: The aorta carries oxygenated blood from the left ventricle.
whyNot.3: Both of these vessels carry oxygenated blood.

C.q: Deoxygenated blood from the heart muscle drains through the coronary veins into the:
options: Coronary sinus, then the left atrium
Pulmonary veins, then the left atrium
Coronary sinus, then the right atrium
Superior vena cava, then the right ventricle
C.why: Coronary veins collect into the coronary sinus, which empties into the right atrium along with the venae cavae.

whyNot.0: The coronary sinus empties into the RIGHT atrium, which receives all deoxygenated blood.
whyNot.1: Pulmonary veins carry oxygenated blood from the lungs, not blood from the heart muscle.
whyNot.3: The superior vena cava empties into the right atrium, not the right ventricle, and does not drain the heart muscle.

reteach.title: A figure-eight track
reteach.question: Picture a figure-eight race track with a pit stop where the two loops cross. How does that shape match the pulmonary and systemic circulations?

blocks.body: The heart is the crossing point of a figure eight. The small loop runs to the lungs and back: cars (red blood cells) leave from the right side tired and come back to the left side refueled with oxygen. The big loop runs around the whole body: cars leave from the left side full and come back to the right side empty. Every car must drive both loops, one after the other, forever.

blocks.text: On the small loop the names flip expectations: pulmonary arteries leave the heart carrying "empty" (deoxygenated) blood, and pulmonary veins return "full" (oxygenated) blood.

explain.body: Right ventricle, pulmonary valve, pulmonary trunk, pulmonary arteries, lung capillaries (O₂ in, CO₂ out), pulmonary veins, left atrium.

test.q: The pulmonary circulation carries blood from the:
options: Right ventricle to the lungs to the left atrium
Left ventricle to the lungs to the right atrium
Right atrium to the lungs to the left ventricle
Right ventricle to the body to the left atrium
test.why: The pulmonary circuit starts at the right ventricle, passes through the lungs and ends at the left atrium.

whyNot.1: The left ventricle starts the systemic circuit, which ends at the right atrium.
whyNot.2: Blood goes RA to RV before the lungs, and returns to the left ATRIUM, not ventricle.
whyNot.3: The pulmonary circuit goes to the lungs, not the body.

explain.body: Pulmonary veins, left atrium, mitral valve, left ventricle, aortic valve, aorta, then arteries, arterioles, capillaries, venules, veins and the venae cavae back to the right atrium.

test.q: Which valve does blood cross as it leaves the left ventricle?
options: Mitral valve
Pulmonary valve
Aortic valve
Tricuspid valve
test.why: Blood exits the left ventricle through the aortic semilunar valve into the aorta.

whyNot.0: The mitral valve is the ENTRY to the left ventricle from the left atrium.
whyNot.1: The pulmonary valve is the exit from the right ventricle.
whyNot.3: The tricuspid valve is on the right side, between RA and RV.

explain.body: Arteries carry blood away from the heart; veins carry it toward the heart, regardless of oxygen. So pulmonary arteries carry deoxygenated blood and pulmonary veins carry oxygenated blood.

test.q: The pulmonary arteries are classed as arteries because they:
options: Carry oxygen-rich blood to the lungs
Carry blood away from the heart
Have valves that prevent backflow
Carry blood at the lowest pressure
test.why: Any vessel carrying blood away from the heart is an artery, even when the blood is deoxygenated.

whyNot.0: Pulmonary arteries carry oxygen-POOR blood to the lungs.
whyNot.2: Valves along the vessel are a feature of veins, not the basis for naming arteries.
whyNot.3: Arteries carry blood at higher pressure; low pressure describes veins.

explain.body: Coronary arteries leave the base of the aorta and fill mainly during diastole; coronary veins drain to the coronary sinus and right atrium. The hepatic portal vein carries blood from the gut, spleen and pancreas to the liver before the heart.

test.q: The coronary arteries receive most of their blood flow during:
options: Systole, while the heart contracts
Atrial systole, as the atria contract
Systole, as the aortic valve opens
Diastole, while the heart relaxes
test.why: Coronary arteries fill mainly during diastole, when the relaxed heart muscle is not squeezing them.

whyNot.0: During systole the contracting myocardium squeezes the coronary vessels, limiting flow.
whyNot.1: Atrial systole is a brief part of the cycle and is not when most coronary filling happens.
whyNot.2: When the aortic valve opens the ventricles are contracting, which limits coronary flow.
